details.description: Nova-3 is Deepgram's current-generation general-purpose speech-to-text model, recommended for meetings, event captioning, multi-speaker, multilingual, noisy, or far-field audio in both batch and streaming. Calling the API with `model=nova-3` uses the same default "general" option documented as `nova-3-general`; Deepgram also offers nova-3-medical and nova-3-pharma variants for healthcare and pharmaceutical vocabulary. Deepgram's changelog shows the Nova-3 family under active development through September 2026, including new monolingual language updates and the addition of nova-3-pharma.
advantages: Deepgram reports a 53.4% reduction in word error rate for real-time streaming and a 47.4% reduction for batch transcription compared to the competitors it tested, per its documentation.
Supports real-time multilingual transcription with code-switching across English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Russian, Portuguese, Japanese, Italian, and Dutch within a single conversation.
Deepgram describes it as the first of its voice AI models to offer self-serve vocabulary customization, letting users adapt to new terms without retraining the model.
Includes an optional personal-information redaction feature, per Deepgram's documentation.
disadvantages: This general option is not tuned for medical or pharmaceutical vocabulary; Deepgram offers separate nova-3-medical and nova-3-pharma variants for those domains.
use_cases: General-purpose transcription of meetings, events, and multi-speaker conversations in noisy or far-field conditions.
Real-time multilingual transcription with code-switching for customer support or contact-center audio.
Batch transcription of recorded audio that needs custom vocabulary adapted without retraining.

sources.title: Introducing Nova-3: Setting a New Standard for AI-Driven Speech-to-Text
Nova-3 Improved Models for Danish, Estonian, Flemish, Italian, Lithuanian, Macedonian, Polish, Urdu, and Vietnamese | Deepgram's Docs

notes: developers.deepgram.com/docs/model documents model=nova-3-{option} with general/medical/pharma as the only listed options, and models-languages-overview lists `nova-3` and `nova-3-general` together in the same language-support table row, so this entry treats nova-3 (bare) and nova-3-general as the same model. The current docs/model page states a 53.4%/47.4% WER reduction; Deepgram's original October 2024 launch post (introducing-nova-3-speech-to-text-api) instead states 54.2% streaming / 47.4% batch with median WERs of 6.84% and 5.26%, and the also-current models-languages-overview page still shows that same older 54.2% figure too -- docs/model (the dedicated model-options page) is treated as the more authoritative, updated number, so 53.4% is the one used here. WER figures are not included in evaluations since they are not accuracy-style, higher-is-better scores. Language list is Deepgram's stated per-language support for nova-3-general; only the 10 languages named above support real-time code-switching. No evaluations entries were found in the required 0-100 higher-is-better format (only WER figures, which the brief excludes). The 'changelog...active development...monolingual language updates' claim was originally cited only to the Sept 17 nova-3-pharma changelog entry, which does not itself mention language updates; added the Sept 22, 2026 changelog entry ('improved Nova-3 monolingual models for nine existing languages') as direct support.
